body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: No test coverage for any of the 4 verification criteria. Searched src/services/__tests__/ for 'live_preview|preview|draft|management_token' — zero matches. VC1 (options.live_preview shape), VC2 (draft content rendered when preview params present), VC3 (published content no regressions when params absent), and VC4 (API requests include/omit preview params) are all untested. The existing test file covers fetch timeout config and query methods but has no live_preview assertions whatsoever.
issues.suggestedFix: Add test cases to src/services/__tests__/contentstack.spec.ts: (1) Assert options.live_preview equals { enable: true, host: expect.any(String) }. (2) Mock the Contentstack Stack to return draft entries and verify they surface through getEntry/getSingleEntry when live_preview query params are present. (3) Assert that when no preview params exist, the query path is unchanged (existing tests partially cover this but none assert the absence of preview params in the SDK calls). (4) Verify the Stack initialization passes live_preview config to contentstack.Stack().

issues.description: The `as unknown as Config` double-cast bypasses TypeScript's type system entirely, masking any real type mismatch between the options object and the SDK's expected Config type. This cast is NOT part of the prescribed minimal fix and adds unnecessary complexity. The Config type is imported solely to enable this unsafe cast. If the options object genuinely doesn't match Config, the correct approach is to align the object's type (e.g., annotate `options` with the SDK's expected type or fix the shape), not to silence the compiler with a double assertion.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the `Config` import and the `as unknown as Config` cast. If TypeScript complains about the options type, either (a) type the options object explicitly as `contentstack.Config` and fix any shape mismatches, or (b) if the SDK's types are stale/incorrect, add a targeted `// @ts-expect-error` with an explanatory comment on the specific property that mismatches — not a blanket double-cast of the entire object.

issues.description: `management_token` was removed from the live_preview config, but dependency_contract confirms the contentstack SDK (v3.17.2) consumes `management_token` within the live_preview configuration. The SDK uses this token to authenticate requests for draft/unpublished content during live preview. Without it, VC2 ('rendered page displays draft content from those entries') may fail at runtime — the SDK may be unable to fetch unpublished entries without the management token. While the prescribed fix omits it, the dependency contract evidence suggests this is a functional risk.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore `management_token: CONTENTSTACK_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN || ''` to the live_preview config object and re-add `CONTENTSTACK_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` to the destructured env vars. If the token is genuinely unnecessary, add a comment citing evidence (e.g., SDK docs or runtime test proving draft content is fetched without it).

issues.description: The `Config` type import (`import contentstack, { Config } from "contentstack"`) is added solely to support the unsafe double-cast on line 69. If the cast is removed (as recommended), this import becomes unused and should also be removed, reverting to the original `import contentstack from "contentstack"`.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert the import to `import contentstack from "contentstack"` once the double-cast is removed.

VC3: no test verifies published content displays with no regressions when live_preview params are absent (existing tests cover the non-preview path but none assert the absence of live_preview params in API requests). VC4: no test verifies that API requests include live preview parameters from the URL when present and omit them when absent. While VC2–VC4 are partly SDK-driven, the test suite should at minimum verify that the Stack is initialized with `live_preview.enable: true` (which gates the SDK's preview data pipeline) and that the config does not interfere with existing query behavior.

If the original code compiled without the cast, these additions are superfluous and reduce type safety. If a type error prompted the cast, the root cause should be addressed (e.g., the SDK's `Config` type may not declare `live_preview` even though the runtime consumes it — confirmed by dependency_contract as 'consumed' in runtime but potentially absent from .d.ts).

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Root cause not addressed — getContentByKey calls Stack.livePreviewQuery() as a fire-and-forget side effect but then returns the same static published content via getValue(content, path, defaultValue). The return value of livePreviewQuery is completely discarded. The prescribed fix says to 'merge or replace the static content lookup with a live preview fetch when preview mode is active.' This implementation does neither — it calls livePreviewQuery and ignores its result, then returns published content. VC1 ('rendered page displays the draft version') and VC2 ('updates in real time') are not met because draft content is never returned.
issues.suggestedFix: Capture the result of the live preview fetch and return it (or merge it with the static content) instead of always returning getValue(content, path, defaultValue). When livePreview is active, getContentByKey should resolve to the draft content from the preview SDK response, not the static context object.

issues.description: Stack.livePreviewQuery does not exist on the Contentstack SDK Stack object. CodeGraph query for 'livePreviewQuery' returned no results. The Stack object is contentstack.Stack(options) from the Contentstack delivery SDK (src/services/contentstack.ts:69) and has no livePreviewQuery method. This would cause a TypeScript compile error (property does not exist on type) or a runtime TypeError. The tests pass only because Stack is fully mocked in the test file.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the actual Contentstack live preview SDK API (e.g., Stack.livePreviewQuery from @contentstack/live-preview-utils or the correct method from the Contentstack SDK). Verify the method exists on the real Stack object before calling it. If the SDK needs configuration (live_preview options with enable, host, management_token), that must be set up in src/services/contentstack.ts first.

issues.description: Unnecessary component-level change — the prescribed minimal fix explicitly states 'all 236+ consumers get preview support with zero component-level changes.' Modifying ContentstackLink to append live_preview to hrefs is a component-level change that should not be needed if useContent properly returns draft content. This violates the concision/reuse criterion: a more concise change (fixing useContent only) would meet the same acceptance criteria.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the ContentstackLink changes entirely. If useContent correctly returns draft content in preview mode, ContentstackLink will automatically render the draft href value with no component modification needed.

issues.description: Tests do not verify the actual acceptance criteria. The test 'enables live preview and calls livePreviewQuery' asserts that livePreviewQuery is *called* with the right params, but never verifies that draft content is actually *returned* by getContentByKey. The mock for Stack.livePreviewQuery returns undefined (jest.fn() with no return value), and getValue is mocked to return from the static content object. No test asserts that getContentByKey returns draft content different from the published content. VC1, VC2 are not demonstrably met by these tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Add tests that mock livePreviewQuery to return draft content data, then assert getContentByKey returns the draft value (not the published value from context). Add a test verifying that when preview params change (simulating a CMS draft update), getContentByKey returns the updated draft value. Assert the actual return value of getContentByKey, not just that livePreviewQuery was called.

issues.description: No real-time subscription mechanism — the prescribed fix says to 'fetch/subscribe to draft content.' The implementation only does a synchronous call inside getContentByKey with no subscription or event listener for real-time updates. VC2 ('updates in real time without a manual page refresh') requires a subscription pattern, not a one-time fetch per render.
issues.suggestedFix: Implement a subscription to the Contentstack live preview SDK's update events (e.g., via useEffect with cleanup) so that when the CMS pushes a draft update, the hook state updates and triggers a re-render with the new draft content.

issues.description: Test file uses jest.mock/jest.fn/jest.clearAllMocks but the project uses vitest. While vitest has jest compatibility mode, the review criteria specify vitest unit tests. Confirm the project's vitest config supports jest-compatible globals, or convert to vi.mock/vi.fn/vi.clearAllMocks.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace jest.* with vi.* from vitest, or confirm the project's vitest configuration has globals: true and jest compatibility enabled.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The prescribed minimal fix explicitly states 'all 236+ consumers get preview support with zero component-level changes.' This diff modifies ContentstackLink.tsx, adding a duplicated isPreviewMode() function and preview detection logic — exactly what the prescribed fix says is unnecessary. Additionally, the old code appended live_preview hash to link URLs (preserving preview state across navigation); the new code removes this and replaces it with a data-cs-preview attribute, which is a functional regression. The hook-level change in useContent.ts already handles preview for all consumers.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert ContentstackLink.tsx entirely. The useContent hook enhancement alone is sufficient per the prescribed fix. If a data-cs-preview attribute is genuinely needed, it should be driven by useContent, not by re-implementing preview detection in each component.

issues.description: Hardcoded string "live_preview" violates criterion 6 (no hardcoded strings — all use named constants). The same constant PREVIEW_HASH_KEY already exists in useContent.ts. This is also a DRY violation — isPreviewMode is already defined in useContent.ts with the named constant.
issues.suggestedFix: If this function is needed (it shouldn't be per the prescribed fix), export isPreviewMode and PREVIEW_HASH_KEY from useContent.ts or a shared constants file and import them. Do not duplicate.

issues.description: Renaming isPreview to previewMode on IContentCard is an unnecessary component-level interface change not prescribed by the root cause analysis. The prescribed fix says the change should be localized to the useContent hook. This field is not used by the hook enhancement. If any existing code references isPreview, this is a silent breaking change.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert this change. The hook-based approach does not require any interface modifications.

issues.description: useContent has no explicit return type annotation: `export const useContent = () => {`. The old code returned IUseContentReturn. This violates TypeScript strict compliance (all function return types explicitly typed). The inferred return type is fragile — any change to the returned object shape silently changes the public API.
issues.suggestedFix: Define and annotate the return type explicitly, e.g., `export const useContent = (): IUseContentReturn => {` with an updated IUseContentReturn interface that reflects the new shape (just getContentByKey).

issues.description: Security vulnerability: the module-level postMessage listener processes event.data without validating event.origin. Any malicious page or iframe can dispatch a message with type 'contentstack-live-preview' and inject arbitrary content into the rendered page. This is an OWASP concern (untrusted origin processing postMessage data).
issues.suggestedFix: Add origin validation against a known Contentstack origin (from constants), e.g., `if (event.origin !== CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ORIGIN) return;` before processing the message. The origin should be a named constant from src/config/constants.ts.

issues.description: Module-scoped previewOverlay and previewListeners have no reset mechanism and are not exported. This makes the overlay state impossible to clean between test runs, leading to cross-test contamination. The test file itself acknowledges this: 'module-scoped state persists across renders.' The test 'returns draft content from overlay when live preview mode is active' depends on state leaked from a prior test's act() call.
issues.suggestedFix: Export a __resetPreviewOverlay function for test use (guarded by NODE_ENV), or restructure to use a class/singleton with a reset method. At minimum, add a beforeEach reset in the test file.

issues.description: The postMessage listener is registered at module load time as a side effect. This is an anti-pattern — module side effects make the code harder to test, harder to tree-shake, and can cause issues in SSR environments. The listener is never removed.
issues.suggestedFix: Register the listener inside the hook's useEffect (or a lazy initializer) so it's bound to the React lifecycle and properly cleaned up. Alternatively, use a ref-counted approach where the listener is added when the first consumer mounts and removed when the last unmounts.

issues.description: The getContentByKey uses Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(previewOverlay, path) to check if the overlay has a value for the exact path key. But getValue supports nested dot-notation paths (e.g., 'hero.title'). The overlay stores top-level content fields (e.g., 'hero_title'), not nested paths. If a component requests 'hero.title' but the overlay has { hero: { title: 'Draft' } }, the hasOwnProperty check fails and published content is returned instead of the draft. The check should use getValue to resolve the path and compare against the default value, or the overlay should be checked differently.
issues.suggestedFix: In preview mode, always call getValue on the overlay first and only fall back to published content if the overlay returns undefined/default. E.g.: `if (isPreviewMode()) { const draftValue = getValue(previewOverlay, path, undefined); if (draftValue !== undefined) return draftValue as T; } return getValue(content, path, defaultValue);`

issues.description: The overlay merge is shallow: `previewOverlay = { ...previewOverlay, ...data.content }`. If Contentstack sends partial nested object updates, entire nested structures will be replaced rather than deep-merged, potentially losing sibling fields that were present in a previous draft update.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a deep merge utility if partial nested updates are expected, or document that Contentstack always sends complete content objects.

issues.description: The test 'updates rendered content in real time when a new draft value arrives via postMessage' asserts valueAfter !== valueBefore, but valueBefore may already be 'Updated Draft' if module-scoped state leaked from a prior test. The assertion is fragile and order-dependent. The test comment even acknowledges this: 'module-scoped state persists across renders.'
issues.suggestedFix: Reset the module-scoped overlay before each test, or assert against a known initial value rather than relying on valueBefore being different.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: ContentstackLink is over-engineered. The prescribed fix explicitly states 'zero component-level changes' — all 236+ consumers should get preview support through the hook alone. The only required change here is removing the now-removed `livePreview`/`previewHash` destructuring and the `finalHref` computation. Instead, 12+ lines were added: a duplicated `isPreviewMode` function, `useState`, `useEffect`, and a `data-cs-preview` attribute that appears in no acceptance criterion. A more concise change: `const { getContentByKey } = useContent(); const { href } = getContentByKey(contentKey, {} as IContentstackLink); return <CustomLink {...props} href={href} className={linkClasses}>{children}</CustomLink>;`
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `isPreviewMode`, `useState`, `useEffect`, and the `data-cs-preview` spread. Keep only the minimal diff: remove `livePreview`/`previewHash` from destructuring, remove `finalHref`, use `href` directly.

issues.description: `isPreviewMode` is hand-rolled identically in two files: `useContent.ts` (line 22) and `ContentstackLink.tsx` (line 5). This violates the concision/reuse rule — the function already exists in `useContent.ts` and should be exported and imported rather than duplicated.
issues.suggestedFix: Export `isPreviewMode` from `useContent.ts` and import it in `ContentstackLink.tsx` (if still needed after removing the over-engineered changes).

issues.description: Missing explicit return type on `useContent`. The old code declared `(): IUseContentReturn`. The new code has no return type annotation, relying on inference. TypeScript strict compliance requires all function return types to be explicitly typed. The exported `IUseContentReturn` interface was also removed, which is a breaking change for any consumer importing it.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an explicit return type interface (e.g., `IUseContentReturn` with `getContentByKey`) and annotate the function: `export const useContent = (): IUseContentReturn => {`.

issues.description: Implementation deviates from the prescribed minimal fix, which states: 'use Contentstack's live preview SDK to fetch/subscribe to draft content for the given contentKey.' The old code used `Stack.livePreviewQuery()` from `services/contentstack`. The new implementation removes the SDK import entirely and replaces it with a custom `window.postMessage` listener. While the postMessage approach may functionally work for iframe-based previews, it does not use the Contentstack SDK as prescribed and may not integrate with Contentstack's actual preview protocol.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify whether Contentstack's live preview SDK provides a postMessage-based API or a programmatic fetch API. If the SDK provides a method to subscribe to draft content, use it instead of the hand-rolled postMessage listener. If postMessage IS the SDK's protocol, document this in the code comment.

issues.description: Renaming `isPreview` to `previewMode` is unnecessary scope creep. The prescribed fix is localized to `useContent.ts`. A search confirmed `isPreview` was never used in `src/`, so the rename is safe but adds diff noise without addressing the root cause.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert this change unless there is a specific reason the rename is needed for the preview feature.

issues.description: Module-scoped `previewOverlay` is never cleared. While functionally safe (guarded by `isPreviewMode()`), this causes test isolation issues — the overlay persists across test cases, making tests order-dependent. The test in 'returns draft content from overlay' relies on state from a prior test's postMessage dispatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Export a `resetPreviewOverlay` function (or use a class/closure pattern) and call it in `beforeEach` in the test file. Alternatively, clear the overlay when `isPreviewMode()` transitions from true to false.

issues.description: The `useEffect` that registers the preview listener has an empty dependency array `[]`, meaning it only runs on mount. If a user enters preview mode after the component has mounted (e.g., by changing the URL hash without navigation), the re-render listener won't be registered. `getContentByKey` still checks `isPreviewMode()` on every call so content resolution is correct, but real-time updates won't trigger re-renders in this edge case.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `isPreviewMode()` as a dependency or re-check preview mode on hash change events.
